ai.description: This slender colubrid reaches 60 cm. It is brown or reddish-grey with dark mottling. Key features include a triangular, shovel-shaped head and large, forward-facing eyes with vertical pupils.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Psammodynastes pulverulentus* is its distinct, shovel-shaped, flattened snout combined with large, vertically elliptical pupils.
ai.habitat: The Common Mock Viper inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, typically ranging from lowlands up to 2,000 meters in elevation across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: When threatened, the Common Mock Viper flattens its neck and strikes repeatedly with its mouth open to mimic the defensive display of a much larger, dangerous viper.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Psammodynastes pulverulentus* is ovoviviparous, typically producing a litter of 3–10 young. Breeding occurs throughout the year, peaking during the monsoon season in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Common Mock Viper occurs in Northeast India, including states like Assam and Arunachal Pradesh, inhabiting tropical forests from lowlands up to 2,000 meters elevation.
